nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be a positive definite symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with integer entries, with quadratic form $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$. Then $Q$ is universal, that is, it represents every positive integer, if and only if it represents every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le 15$.
nodes.title: Conway–Schneeberger fifteen theorem

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$ and an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$, the value of the quadratic form of $M$ at a vector $x \in R^n$ is $x \cdot (M x) = \sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j$, where $i$ and $j$ range over $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of a matrix

nodes.summary: For an $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries, the quadratic form of $Q$ is the map $\mathbb{Z}^n \to \mathbb{Z}$ sending $x$ to $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$, where $i$ and $j$ range over $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. No symmetry of $Q$ is assumed.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of an integer matrix

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ is integral if its quadratic form takes integer values at integer vectors: for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the value $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j$ computed in $R$ lies in the image of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $R$.
nodes.title: Integer-valued quadratic forms

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ is universal if it represents every positive integer: for every positive integer $m$ there is $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j = m$ in $R$.
nodes.title: Universal quadratic forms over a ring

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries is universal if its quadratic form $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$ represents every positive integer, that is, for every positive integer $m$ there is $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $Q(x) = m$.
nodes.title: Universal integer-matrix quadratic forms

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ represents a natural number $m$ if there is an integer vector $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j = m$, where the entries of $x$ and the number $m$ are viewed as elements of $R$.
nodes.title: Natural numbers represented by a quadratic form

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries represents an integer $m$ if $Q(x) = m$ for some $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, where $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$.
nodes.title: Integers represented by an integer-matrix quadratic form

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $M$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix that is positive definite (symmetric, with $x^{\top} M x > 0$ for every nonzero $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$) and integral (for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the value $x^{\top} M x$ is an integer). conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.
